Neutrino-nucleus cross section measurements are essential for precision neutrino oscillation experiments and searches for physics beyond the Standard Model.
Modeling neutrino-nucleus interactions is challenging due to the interplay of electroweak and non-perturbative strong forces in a complex nuclear environment at GeV energies.
Event generators like GENIE, NEUT, NuWro, and GiBUU simulate neutrino interactions using collections of effective models.
Cross section extraction involves unfolding reconstructed detector data to true physical quantities using a model-dependent smearing matrix.
Mis-modeling in event generators can bias cross section measurements by affecting background predictions, selection efficiencies, and detector response corrections.
Data-driven model validation techniques use goodness-of-fit tests and correlations between different observables to detect relevant mis-modeling.
Fake data studies demonstrate that data-driven validation can detect model deficiencies and keep biases within quoted uncertainties.
Cross section measurements extracted in the real neutrino flux spectrum reduce dependence on neutrino energy to visible kinematics mapping but require theorists to supply flux models for comparison.
Measurements in the nominal neutrino flux spectrum require extrapolation from the real flux and introduce model dependence in flux uncertainties.
The smearing matrix U describes the probability of reconstructed events belonging to true bins, accounting for detector effects.
The paper uses the MicroBooNE experiment's data and tuning of GENIE with CCQE and 2p2h parameters as a test case.
Selection efficiencies can vary substantially with particle kinematics and final state content, making them sensitive to model assumptions.
Cross section measurements as functions of visible variables like muon energy and angle are less model-dependent than those relying on neutrino energy reconstruction.
The paper emphasizes the importance of including flux shape uncertainties and their correlations in cross section covariance matrices.
Current event generators often require large systematic uncertainties due to incomplete modeling of exclusive final states.
The MicroBooNE collaboration has previously applied data-driven validation techniques in several analyses.
The paper provides a formalism for cross section extraction incorporating flux, detector, and interaction model components.
Mis-modeling can affect background channels and adjacent observables, complicating efficiency and purity estimates.
The paper distinguishes between real and nominal flux cross section extractions and their respective model dependence.
Data-driven model validation helps build confidence that extracted cross sections are robust and unbiased within uncertainties.
